2609.09791.title: MUCnoHARM@GermEval Shared Task 2026: Retrieval-based In-Context Learning for Defamatory Offences, and Where It Falls Short
2609.09791.paper_summary: With hate speech being ubiquitous online, automatic detection is crucial, in particular when it comes to criminally relevant social media posts. We study a variety of retrieval-based in-context learning (RetICL) strategies for detecting defamatory offences under §§ 185-187 StGB (the subject of GermEval 2026 Subtask 4). Few-shot prompting beats zero-shot, but retrieval-based approaches offer only marginal gains over random demonstrations, and even fall behind an optimised static set of demonstrations. Providing concrete legal knowledge helps, yet model choice outweighs every other system choice. Models over-predict criminal relevance while still missing 26-57% of criminally relevant posts, suiting them for triage rather than autonomous moderation.
2609.09791.paper_summary_zh: 隨著仇恨言論在網路上無處不在，自動檢測變得至關重要，特別是在涉及刑事相關的社交媒體帖子時。我們研究了多種基於檢索的上下文學習（RetICL）策略，以檢測根據《德國刑法》第185-187條的誹謗罪（這是GermEval 2026子任務4的主題）。少量提示優於零提示，但基於檢索的方法僅比隨機示範提供邊際增益，甚至不如優化的靜態示範集。提供具體的法律知識有幫助，但模型選擇超過了其他所有系統選擇。模型過度預測刑事相關性，但仍然錯過了26-57%的刑事相關帖子，使它們適合於篩選而非自動管理。
2609.09791.author: Kristin Gnadt et.al.
